description: Hi! I'm M. Ayshwarya, an engineering student interested in space exploration, astronomy, software development, and data analysis. I'm excited to contribute to the NASA Space Apps Challenge by exploring Earth locations that could serve as analogs for future Moon and Mars bases. I'm looking for teammates with skills in planetary science, geology, GIS and mapping, coding, data visualization, and creative problem-solving. Let's collaborate and build an innovative solution!
summary:
TERRAOPS, developed by Team Cosmic Catalyst, is an interactive spatial and temporal intelligence platform designed to identify and evaluate Earth environments for future Mars mission rehearsals. It compares Jezero Crater on Mars with three potential terrestrial analogues: the Atacama Desert, Ladakh and Askja, Iceland.
Using open NASA and Earth-observation datasets, TERRAOPS brings together terrain analysis, slope and surface roughness comparisons, rover-mobility considerations and temperature assessments. Its interactive maps and comparison tools help users explore the similarities and differences between Martian and terrestrial environments. The “When-to-Test” module investigates periods when Earth temperature conditions align with a defined Martian reference envelope, while the Analogy Gap Detector highlights environmental differences, data limitations and scientific uncertainties.
Rather than treating any Earth location as an exact replica of Mars, TERRAOPS provides a transparent, data-driven framework for understanding where and when terrestrial environments can support planetary exploration research. By transforming complex datasets into accessible, meaningful insights, the platform aims to support better-informed site assessments, mission rehearsals and the preparation of future robotic and human exploration of Mars.
details:
TERRAOPS is an interactive spatial and temporal intelligence platform developed by Team Cosmic Catalyst to identify and evaluate terrestrial environments that can serve as useful analogues for future Mars mission rehearsals. The platform compares Jezero Crater, Mars, with three Earth locations: the Atacama Desert in Chile, Ladakh in India, and Askja in Iceland.

The project works by integrating open planetary and Earth-observation datasets into a unified analytical framework. It examines terrain characteristics, including elevation, slope and surface roughness, considers rover mobility requirements, and compares temperature behaviour using available observations. Interactive maps, site profiles and comparison visualisations allow users to explore each candidate environment. The “When-to-Test” module investigates when Earth temperature observations fall within a defined Martian reference envelope, while the Analogy Gap Detector identifies differences, uncertainties and limitations that may affect the suitability of each analogue.

TERRAOPS was developed using Python and Streamlit, supported by geospatial analysis, data processing and visualisation workflows. The team worked with NASA planetary and environmental datasets, including Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer (MEDA) observations, NASA MODIS Land Surface Temperature data, NASA POWER and Copernicus elevation products. QGIS supported the geographic and terrain-analysis workflow.

The creative aspect of TERRAOPS lies in bringing spatial comparison, temporal assessment and scientific uncertainty into one accessible platform rather than relying only on visual similarities between landscapes. The team considered terrain conditions, rover mobility, temperature comparability, data availability, spatial resolution, measurement quality and the limitations of Earth-based simulations.

The intended impact is to support more transparent and evidence-based selection of terrestrial analogue environments, helping researchers identify useful locations and testing periods while recognising what Earth cannot fully reproduce. TERRAOPS aims to contribute to better-prepared robotic and human exploration missions to Mars.
